title: A closed line stamps its close date; a service completes via any of five paths
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with View and edit customers, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. A service is due or overdue on an enrolled asset (e.g. 'PM-A' on unit 'ZZAUTOTEST Truck 12').
custom_steps:
1. Close a line and confirm it stamps the date it closed, visible on the work order and distinct from the invoice date.
  2. Confirm a service added by canned lines completes when every line it added completes, and a service marked complete without lines completes when it is marked.
  3. Confirm line completion counts via any of the five paths: completing the line, the bulk action bar, creating an invoice, clocking out, and review.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Each closed line stamps the date it closed, visible on the work order and distinct from the invoice date.
  • A service added by its canned lines completes when every line it added completes; a service marked complete without lines completes when it is marked.
  • Line completion counts by any of the five paths: completing the line, the bulk action bar, creating an invoice, clocking out, and review.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10574 (S18, Complete a service and reset the cycle); Chunk 2 MR spec (Confluence 897679389), Part 1 / S18; read 2 Oct 2026. Source-verified 2 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S18-R9: “Each closed line will stamp the date it closed, visible on the work order and distinct from the invoice date”
  • S18-R10: “A service added by its canned lines completes when every line it added completes. A service marked complete without lines completes when it is marked. The spec means line completion by any of the five paths that reach it: completing the line, the bulk action bar, creating an invoice, clocking out, and review”
